boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten no-purchase Lafayette College activities spanning public art, current history exhibitions, and student recreation.

cards.title: Browse the Williams Center Gallery
cards.subtitle: A free public exhibition stop on College Hill
cards.notes: Meet at the Williams Center, browse the current exhibition together, and leave time to compare favorite works before closing.
cards.short_summary: A public gallery hang built around rotating exhibitions in the Williams Center for the Arts.
cards.evidence_claim: Lafayette states that its exhibitions and related programming are free and open to the public; the visitor guide lists Williams Center Gallery at 317 Hamilton Street.
cards.access_notes: Open to the public during posted gallery hours; check the visitor guide because galleries close for holidays and campus closures.

cards.entity_name: Richard A. and Rissa W. Grossman Gallery
cards.title: See Contemporary Art at Grossman Gallery
cards.subtitle: A free downtown gallery visit for campus and community
cards.notes: Walk down College Hill with friends, explore the current installation, and use the exhibit as an easy conversation starter.
cards.short_summary: A no-admission contemporary-art outing at Lafayette’s Williams Visual Arts Building.
cards.evidence_claim: Lafayette identifies Grossman Gallery as one of its gallery locations and states that exhibitions and related programming are free and open to the public.
cards.access_notes: Open to the public during posted hours at 243 N. Third Street; the gallery closes for most academic holidays.

cards.title: Look Closely at the Kirby Art Study Center
cards.subtitle: A free, small-group art stop inside the Williams Center
cards.notes: Bring a classmate, focus on a few collection works, and trade observations instead of trying to cover everything at once.
cards.short_summary: A quieter public art-viewing option centered on close study of Lafayette’s collection.
cards.evidence_claim: The official visitor guide lists Kirby Art Study Center among Lafayette’s galleries and says gallery exhibitions and related programming are free and open to the public.
cards.access_notes: Visit Wednesday through Friday during posted hours or arrange an appointment; campus closures and holidays may affect access.

cards.title: Follow the Campus Sculpture Walk
cards.subtitle: A self-guided outdoor art loop across Lafayette’s grounds
cards.notes: Open the official map, choose a cluster of sculptures, and take turns reading the artist notes while walking between works.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor, self-paced route linking public sculptures around Lafayette’s campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Lafayette’s Art on Campus page provides a self-guided sculpture walk and says the mapped outdoor sculptures include descriptions and artist-biography links.
cards.source_title: Art On Campus · Lafayette Art Galleries
cards.access_notes: The route uses outdoor public sculptures on campus grounds and requires no gallery ticket or reservation.

cards.entity_name: This Incomparable Site: From College Edifice to College Hill
cards.title: Trace How College Hill Took Shape
cards.subtitle: A free architecture-history exhibition in Skillman Library
cards.notes: Start in Lass Gallery, compare early campus images with today’s surroundings, then step outside to spot what changed.
cards.short_summary: A visual history hang using engravings, maps, and photographs of Lafayette’s built environment.
cards.evidence_claim: Lafayette lists this exhibition in Lass Gallery through December 18, 2026 and states that its bicentennial exhibitions are free and open to the public.
cards.access_notes: Free and open to the public during Skillman Library access hours; the listed run ends December 18, 2026.

cards.entity_name: We’ll Gather by the Twilight’s Glow: 200 Years of Community at Lafayette College
cards.title: Scan Two Centuries of Group Photos
cards.subtitle: A free community-history display in Skillman Library
cards.notes: Browse the panoramic photographs with friends and pick out changes in clothing, ceremonies, and campus gathering places.
cards.short_summary: A social photo-history stop showing Lafayette communities across generations.
cards.evidence_claim: Lafayette lists this Skillman Library exhibition through December 18, 2026 and says the bicentennial exhibitions are free and open to the public.
cards.access_notes: Free and open to the public during Skillman Library access hours; the listed run ends December 18, 2026.

cards.entity_name: Lafayette 200: A Bicentennial History of Lafayette College
cards.title: Explore Lafayette’s Bicentennial History
cards.subtitle: A free document-and-artifact exhibition in the Simon Room
cards.notes: Choose one era to investigate together, examine the displayed documents, and compare what each person notices first.
cards.short_summary: An artifact-centered look at Lafayette’s founding, organizations, conflicts, and institutional changes.
cards.evidence_claim: The College lists Lafayette 200 in Skillman Library’s Simon Room through December 18, 2026 and states that bicentennial exhibitions are free and open to the public.
cards.access_notes: Free and open to the public during applicable Skillman Library and Simon Room hours; the listed run ends December 18, 2026.

cards.title: Meet for a Recreational Swim
cards.subtitle: Student no-cost pool time at Kirby Sports Center
cards.notes: Check the current pool schedule, bring your Lafayette ID and swim gear, and meet on deck for an easy shared workout.
cards.short_summary: A student-only aquatic hang in Lafayette’s six-lane pool and separate diving well.
cards.evidence_claim: Recreation Services describes Lafayette’s recreational swim program and states that students have no-cost facility access with a valid Lafayette ID.
cards.access_notes: Current Lafayette students must present a valid ID, complete the required waiver, and use the pool only during posted recreational-swim hours.

cards.title: Try the Climbing Wall Together
cards.subtitle: A no-cost student climbing session at Kirby Sports Center
cards.notes: Confirm open-climb hours, bring your Lafayette ID, and start with routes suited to the least-experienced person in the group.
cards.short_summary: An indoor student activity where friends can attempt climbing routes at their own pace.
cards.evidence_claim: Recreation Services identifies the Climbing Wall as a Lafayette recreation offering and states that students receive no-cost facility access with valid Lafayette ID.
cards.access_notes: For current Lafayette students with valid ID and completed waiver; check current wall hours and follow staff safety requirements.

cards.title: Take a Group Fitness Class
cards.subtitle: A no-cost student workout through Recreation Services
cards.notes: Pick a class that suits everyone’s comfort level, confirm any sign-up requirement, and arrive early enough to get settled.
cards.short_summary: A structured movement session that turns exercise into an easy campus group plan.
cards.evidence_claim: Lafayette Recreation Services lists Group Fitness among its programs, while its facility-access policy grants students no-cost access with valid Lafayette ID.
cards.access_notes: Limited to current Lafayette students with valid ID and a completed facility waiver; consult the live program schedule before going.
